ho-chi-minh-city.source: prior research, carried over from the project brief
ho-chi-minh-city.bottom_line: District 3 is the Hai Chau equivalent — real residential Saigon with enough cafes and expats to function, without District 1 pricing or crowds.
also_good: Phu Nhuan — hidden gem, more local, cheaper
Binh Thanh — value pick, good for the budget
avoid: District 1 — touristy and priced for it
ho-chi-minh-city.notes: Outdoor fitness, work cafes, and specific listings were never researched in detail. Run a refresh before flying.

chiang-mai.source: prior research, carried over from the project brief
chiang-mai.bottom_line: Santitham is the pick: local, cheap at THB 8,000-18,000/month, and five minutes by scooter to everything Nimman has without paying Nimman rents.
sweet_spot: Santitham — best overall. Local, THB 8,000-18,000/mo, 5 min scooter to Nimman
also_good: Nimman — slightly expat-heavy but the best cafes and gyms
cafes: CAMP Cafe at Maya Mall — open till midnight
chiang-mai.notes: Outdoor pull-up bars were never confirmed here — that is the open question. Burning season (roughly February to April) is the other thing to check before committing to dates.

tokyo.source: prior research, carried over from the project brief
tokyo.bottom_line: Ota-ku along the Tokyu Ikegami line is the residential-Tokyo answer: confirmed outdoor pull-up bars a seven-minute walk away, unhurried Komeda-style cafes, and 20 minutes to Shibuya.
fitness: Yaguchi Nichome Park — 7 min walk, confirmed pull-up bars, known locally as Tarzan Park
Heiwanomori Park — 20 min bike, 40-obstacle outdoor course, 4.1 stars
Den-en-chofu Seseragikan — public community gym, JPY 400/session, 4.3 stars
cafes: Komeda's Coffee Shimomaruko — huge booths, 06:30-22:30, never rushed
Pelican Coffee Den-en-chofu — WiFi and outlets, work-from-home crowd
Kamata Cafe — 4.5 stars, outlets, near-empty on weekdays
tokyo.transit: Tokyu Ikegami line to Kamata, then Shibuya in 20 min or Shinagawa in 15 min.
tokyo.notes: The strongest confirmed fitness finding of any city so far. Housing under $800 for two is the constraint here — verify before committing.

osaka.source: prior research, carried over from the project brief
osaka.bottom_line: Nishinakajima works for transit on the Midosuji line but fails the daily-fitness test — no confirmed pull-up bars within walking distance. Fixable by choosing a different base near Nakatsu or Nagai.
also_good: Nishinakajima / Kita ward — good transit, weak outdoor fitness
fitness: Juso Park — 15 min from Nishinakajima, confirmed bar
Nakatsu South Park — confirmed pull-ups and dip bars
Nagai Park — 9,000+ reviews, running track, pool, skate park
Osaka Castle Park + Running Base — 5km moat loop, locker and shower JPY 1,000
Tsurumi Ryokuchi — free parkrun on Saturdays
osaka.notes: Open question: which neighborhood near Nakatsu South Park or Nagai Park has furnished stock under $800. That is the thing to research next.

seoul.source: prior research, carried over from the project brief
seoul.bottom_line: Seongsu-dong, Yeonnam-dong, or Mangwon-dong give the chill local feel inside Seoul. Chuncheon, an hour east, is the nature option if the city gets heavy.
seoul.notes: Nature nearby: Chuncheon, 1 hr east, lakes and mountains. Outdoor fitness parks are common in Korean neighborhoods but were never confirmed for these specific areas. Budget is the open question — Seoul is the most expensive city on the list.

busan.source: prior research, carried over from the project brief
busan.bottom_line: The best Chiang Mai equivalent in Korea — beach, mountains, and meaningfully cheaper than Seoul.
busan.notes: Nothing confirmed yet on outdoor bars, cafes, or listings. Full scout needed.

fukuoka.source: prior research, carried over from the project brief
fukuoka.bottom_line: Ranked #1 of the Japanese cities as a Chiang Mai equivalent: beach and mountains close, cheapest of the four, great cafes, compact, and direct flights to Southeast Asia.
notes: Japan ranking from the brief, best first:
1. Fukuoka — beach and mountains nearby, cheapest, great cafes, compact, direct SEA flights
2. Kanazawa — Sea of Japan and mountains, ~$415/mo average rent, cultural
4. Sapporo — nature-heavy, ~25% cheaper than Tokyo, cold winters
